66423-a-concise-practical-treatise-on-ar.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Its pliability assists greatly, not only in throwing the fly, but in hooking and retaining the fish. The butt end should have a hollow sufficient to hold an extra top-piece, secured by a brass screw-nut, which, when the rod is used, should be taken out, and a spike [Illustration] screwed into its place.

arxiv-1904-07396.title: Real Image Denoising with Feature Attention
arxiv-1904-07396.creator: Saeed Anwar, Nick Barnes
arxiv-1904-07396.description: Abstract Deep convolutional neural networks perform better on images containing spatially invariant noise (synthetic noise); however, their performance is limited on real-noisy photographs and requires multiple stage network modeling. To advance the practicability of denoising algorithms, this paper proposes a novel single-stage blind real image denoising network (RIDNet) by employing a modular architecture.

arxiv-2102-11392.title: Reinforcement Learning of Beam Codebooks in Millimeter Wave and Terahertz MIMO Systems
arxiv-2102-11392.creator: Yu Zhang, Muhammad Alrabeiah, Ahmed Alkhateeb
arxiv-2102-11392.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yu Zhang, Muhammad Alrabeiah, Ahmed Alkhateeb. Millimeter wave (mmWave) and terahertz MIMO systems rely on pre-defined beamforming codebooks for both initial access and data transmission. Being pre-defined, however, those codebooks are commonly not optimized for specific environments, user distributions, and/or possible hardware impairments. This leads to large codebook sizes with high beam training overhead which increases the initial access/tracking latency and makes it hard for these systems to support highly mobile applications.

arxiv-2106-08242.title: Imprints of high-momentum nucleons in nuclei on hard photons from heavy-ion collisions around the Fermi energy
arxiv-2106-08242.creator: Wen-Mei Guo 1, Bao-An Li 2, Gao-Chan Yong 3
arxiv-2106-08242.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Wen-Mei Guo 1, Bao-An Li 2, Gao-Chan Yong 3. The short-range correlation (SRC) induced by the tensor force in the isosinglet neutron-proton interaction channel leads to a high-momentum tail (HMT) in the single-nucleon momentum distributions n(k) in nuclei.

arxiv-2107-05792.title: What Evidence We Would Miss If We Do Not Use Grey Literature? Conference: ACM / IEEE International Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM); October 11–15, 2021; Bari, Italy ACM / IEEE International Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM) (ESEM ’2
arxiv-2107-05792.creator: Fernando Kamei, Gustavo Pinto, Igor Wiese, Márcio Ribeiro, Sérgio Soares
arxiv-2107-05792.description: Abstract . Context: Over the last years, Grey Literature (GL) is gaining increasing attention in Secondary Studies in Software Engineering (SE). Notably, Multivocal Literature Review (MLR) studies, that search for evidence in both Traditional Literature (TL) and GL, is particularly benefiting from this raise of GL content.

arxiv-2307-06935.title: Collins-type Energy-Energy Correlators and Nucleon Structure
arxiv-2307-06935.creator: Zhong-Bo Kang, Kyle Lee, Ding Yu Shao, and Fanyi Zhao
arxiv-2307-06935.description: Abstract We generalize the conventional Energy-Energy Correlator (EEC) to include the azimuthal angle dependence, so to define azimuthal angle dependent EEC observables. We study this new EEC observable in e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} and semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS).

arxiv-2403-09784.title: Eigenvariety for partially classical Hilbert modular forms
arxiv-2403-09784.creator: Mladen Dimitrov, Chi-Yun Hsu
arxiv-2403-09784.description: Abstract . For each subset of primes in a totally real field above a rational prime p p , there is the notion of partially classical Hilbert modular forms, where the empty set recovers the overconvergent forms and the full set of primes above p p yields classical forms.

arxiv-2407-05924.title: Graph-Boosted Attentive Network for Semantic Body Parsing
arxiv-2407-05924.creator: Tinghuai Wang[0000-0002-7863-3516], Huiling Wang
arxiv-2407-05924.description: Abstract Human body parsing remains a challenging problem in natural scenes due to multi-instance and inter-part semantic confusions as well as occlusions. This paper proposes a novel approach to decomposing multiple human bodies into semantic part regions in unconstrained environments.

arxiv-2409-11453.title: The Puppis A supernova remnant: an early jet-driven neutron star kick followed by jittering jets
arxiv-2409-11453.creator: Ealeal Bear, Dmitry Shishkin, Noam Soker
arxiv-2409-11453.description: Abstract We identify a point-symmetric morphology of three pairs of ears/clumps in the core-collapse supernova remnant (CCSNR) Puppis A, supporting the jittering jets explosion mechanism (JJEM). In the JJEM, the three pairs of jets that shaped the three pairs of ears/clumps in Puppis A are part of a large, about 10 to 30 pairs of jets that exploded Puppis A.

arxiv-2409-18748.title: On NP-Hardness of L 1 / L 2 L_{1}/L_{2} Minimization and Bound Theory of Nonzero Entries in Solutions
arxiv-2409-18748.creator: Min Tao, Xiao-Ping Zhang, Yun-Bin Zhao
arxiv-2409-18748.description: Abstract The L 1 / L 2 L_{1}/L_{2} norm ratio has gained significant attention as a measure of sparsity due to three merits: sharper approximation to the L 0 L_{0} norm compared to the L 1 L_{1} norm, being parameter-free and scale-invariant, and exceptional performance with highly coherent matrices.

arxiv-2503-01129.title: Apollo-MILP: An A lternating P redicti o n-Correction Neura l So l ving Framew o rk for M ixed- I nteger L inear P rogramming
arxiv-2503-01129.creator: Haoyang Liu, Jie Wang, Zijie Geng, Xijun Li, Yuxuan Zong, Fangzhou Zhu, JianYe Hao, Feng Wu
arxiv-2503-01129.description: Abstract Leveraging machine learning (ML) to predict an initial solution for mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) has gained considerable popularity in recent years. These methods predict a solution and fix a subset of variables to reduce the problem dimension. Then, they solve the reduced problem to obtain the final solutions.

arxiv-2511-03117.title: Tracing Generative AI in Digital Art: A Longitudinal Study of Chinese Painters’ Attitudes, Practices, and Identity Negotiation DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X
arxiv-2511-03117.creator: Yibo Meng, Ruiqi Chen, Xin Chen, Zhiming Liu, Yan Guan
arxiv-2511-03117.description: Abstract . This study presents a five-year longitudinal mixed-methods study of 17 Chinese digital painters, examining how their attitudes and practices evolved in response to generative AI. Our findings reveal a trajectory from resistance and defensiveness, to pragmatic adoption, and ultimately to reflective reconstruction, shaped by strong peer pressures and shifting emotional experiences.

arxiv-2511-19028.title: Bell–Plesset Effects on Rayleigh Taylor Instability of Three Dimensional Spherical Geometry
arxiv-2511-19028.creator: Xilai Li, Yilin Wu, Zhengnuo Chen, Mengqi Yang, Jie Zhang
arxiv-2511-19028.description: Abstract We develop a weakly nonlinear, multi-mode theory for the Rayleigh–Taylor instability (RTI) on a time-varying spherical interface, fully incorporating mode couplings and the Bell–Plesset (BP) effects arising from interface convergence. Our model extends prior analyses, which have been largely restricted to static backgrounds, 2D cylindrical geometries, or single-mode initial condition.

arxiv-2602-06892.title: Study of B → K 0 ∗ ​ ( 1430 ) ​ ℓ + ​ ℓ − B\to K_{0}^{*}(1430)\,\ell^{+}\ell^{-} Decay in the Standard Model and Scalar Leptoquark Scenario
arxiv-2602-06892.creator: M. Dadashzadeh, K. Azizi
arxiv-2602-06892.description: Abstract This study examines the rare decay B → K 0 ∗ ​ ( 1430 ) ​ ℓ + ​ ℓ − B\to K_{0}^{*}(1430)\,\ell^{+}\ell^{-} as a possible probe for new physics beyond the standard model (SM). We first analyze this channel within the SM and then include scalar leptoquark (LQ) contributions.

pmc-10513260.title: Can new urbanization and ecological environment achieve synergistic development? Empirical evidence from 63 counties in Zhejiang, China
pmc-10513260.creator: Lindong Ma, Weixiang Xu, Yuanxiao Hong, Shouchao He, Chenjun Liu, Qian Ning
pmc-10513260.description: As China’s urbanization accelerates, ecological environmental issues have become increasingly prominent, and how to achieve the synergistic development of urbanization and ecological environment is worth exploring. The paper uses the Super-SBM model and the improved entropy method to calculate the ecological efficiency and the new urbanization in 63 counties in Zhejiang Province from 2000 to 2019.

pmc-10614130.title: Cellular and molecular characteristics of the premetastatic niches
pmc-10614130.creator: Hongfei Liu, Guoxin Zhang, Ran Gao
pmc-10614130.description: The premetastatic niches (PMN) formed by primary tumor‐derived molecules regulate distant organs and tissues to further favor tumor colonization. Targeted PMN therapy may prevent tumor metastasis in the early stages, which is becoming increasingly important. At present, there is a lack of in‐depth understanding of the cellular and molecular characteristics of the PMN.

pmc-11436667.title: Symbiont community assembly shaped by insecticide exposure and feedback on insecticide resistance of Spodoptera frugiperda
pmc-11436667.creator: Yunhua Zhang, Kaikai Mao, Keyi Chen, Ze Zhao, Feng Ju
pmc-11436667.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Exploring the mechanism of microbiota assembly and its ecological consequences is crucial for connecting microbiome variation to ecosystem function. However, the influencing factors underlying microbiota assembly in the host-microbe system and their impact on the host phenotype remain unclear. Through investigating the prevalent and worsening ecological phenomenon of insecticide resistance in global agriculture, we found that insecticide exposure significantly changed the gut microbiota assembly patterns of a major agricultural invasive insect pest, Spodoptera frugiperda.

pmc-11454515.title: 8592 Parathyroid Carcinoma: A Rare Cause of Primary Hyperparathyroidism
pmc-11454515.creator: S E Koshy, C F Mulcahy, P S Kothari, E M Jacobi, T D Cubb
pmc-11454515.description: Disclosure: S.E. Koshy: None. C.F. Mulcahy: None. P.S. Kothari: None. E.M. Jacobi: None. T.D. Cubb: None. Introduction: Parathyroid carcinoma (PC) is a rare malignancy that accounts for <1% of cases of primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT). Patients often present with symptoms of hypercalcemia, serum calcium (Ca) >14 mg/dL, large tumor size, and a very high parathyroid hormone (PTH) level.

pmc-11468570.title: Hesperidin and Fecal Microbiota Transplantation Modulate the Composition of the Gut Microbiota and Reduce Obesity in High Fat Diet Mice
pmc-11468570.creator: Ting Liu, Chao Lei, Qinhong Huang, Weiqi Song, Chen Li, Ning Sun, Zhihua Liu
pmc-11468570.description: IntroductionObesity, which is associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis, low-grade chronic inflammation and intestinal barrier dysfunction, can cause a variety of chronic metabolic diseases. Phytochemical flavonoids have a variety of biological activities, among which there may be safe and effective anti-obesity solutions.MethodsWe tested a plant-derived flavonoid hesperidin and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) to alleviate diet-induced obesity.

pmc-11651950.title: A multispatial information representation model emphasizing key brain regions for Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis with structural magnetic resonance imaging
pmc-11651950.creator: Pengzhi Nan, Lin Li, Zhiwei Song, Yi Wang, Chuanzhen Zhu, Fang Hu, Qiang Zheng
pmc-11651950.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundStructural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) can reflect structural abnormalities of the brain. Due to its high tissue contrast and spatial resolution, it is considered as an MRI sequence in diagnostic tasks related to Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Thus far, most studies based on sMRI have only focused on pathological changes in disease-related brain regions in Euclidean space, ignoring the association and interaction between brain regions represented in non-Euclidean space. This non-Euclidean spatial information can provide valuable information for brain disease research.

pmc-11665038.title: Violencia obstétrica desde la percepción y vivencias de mujeres en labor de parto, Valledupar, Colombia
pmc-11665038.creator: Margareth Corzo-Contreras, Esther P. Polo-Payares, María C. Murgas-Quintero, Luz A. Hurtado-Luján, Belkis V. Cuesta-Morato
pmc-11665038.description: RESUMENLa violencia obstétrica ha sido definida desde legislaturas de Latinoamérica como todas las acciones u omisiones que el personal de salud ejerce sobre el cuerpo y los procesos reproductivos de las mujeres, consistentes en un trato deshumanizado, abuso de medicalización y patologización, que afecta su experiencia de parto.

pmc-11692735.title: PARTICIPANT EVALUATION OF 4MS EDUCATION DELIVERED BY AGE-FRIENDLY CARE, PA USING PROJECT ECHO: 2020–2023
pmc-11692735.creator: Diane Berish, Jennifer Knecht-Fredo, Erica Husser, Donna Fick, Marie Boltz, Jacqueline Sabol, George Garrow, Angela Houge
pmc-11692735.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Older adults, the largest segment of the US rural population, face significant disparities in health and healthcare compared to their non-rural peers. They have limited access to healthcare and social services for prevention, management, and treatment of chronic conditions. Age-Friendly Care, PA, a collaboration of Primary Health Network, the largest Federally Qualified Health Center in Pennsylvania, and Penn State Nese College of Nursing, aims to bring reliable, high-quality, age-friendly care to all older adults living in rural PA.

pmc-11716448.title: EEG Cortical Sources Abnormalities During Transition Between Wakefulness and Light Sleep in Patients with Alzheimer’s Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment
pmc-11716448.creator: Enrico Michele Salamone, Matteo Carpi, Dharmendra Jakhar, Susanna Lopez, Giuseppe Noce, Roberta Lizio, Claudio Del Percio, Claudio Babiloni
pmc-11716448.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s Disease (AD) and Sleep disturbances are closely linked in a bidirectional relationship. Indeed, sleep alterations represent a precipitating factor in early pathogenesis of neurodegeneration. Conversely, the accumulation of Aβ and tau proteins directly disrupts sleep‐wake cycles. Sleep disturbances are extremely prevalent in AD and the relationship between these disorders has been thoroughly investigated.

pmc-12472628.title: Sorption–Biological Treatment of Coastal Substrates of the Barents Sea in Low Temperature Using the Rhodococcus erythropolis Strain HO-KS22
pmc-12472628.creator: Vladimir Myazin, Maria Korneykova, Nadezhda Fokina, Ekaterina Semenova, Tamara Babich, Milana Murzaeva, O Roger Anderson
pmc-12472628.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The efficiency of the sorption–biological method for treatment of oil-polluted coastal substrates (soil and sand) of the Barents Sea under low temperature (10 °C) using the active hydrocarbon-oxidizing bacterial strain Rhodococcus erythropolis HO-KS22 was assessed in the laboratory. The highest rate of hydrocarbon degradation was in sand polluted with a low-density oil emulsion and in soil polluted with a medium-density oil emulsion.

pmc-13158594.title: Use of wipes with emollient and barrier properties for the prevention of pressure injuries: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
pmc-13158594.creator: Hayley Ryan, Peta Ellen Tehan, Oya Gumuskaya, Alison Hutton, Brett Mitchell
pmc-13158594.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effectiveness of a twice-daily application of a wipe impregnated with emollient and barrier ingredients in reducing incidence of pressure injury (PI) in aged care consumers.DesignA single-blinded, multicentre randomised controlled trial. Randomisation was stratified by facility, using simple 1:1 randomisation within each stratum.

pmc-13227539.title: Social Support and Psychological Capital in Older Adults with Esophageal and Gastric Cancer: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13227539.creator: Amir Hossein Dehghan, Matineh Sadat Tabatabaei, Richard Mottershead, Golnar Ghane
pmc-13227539.description: BackgroundGastrointestinal cancers impose a significant psychological burden on older adults by depleting crucial personal resources. While social support is a known buffer against distress, its specific association with psychological capital (PsyCap) in this population, particularly after the completion of primary treatment, remains under-investigated.

pmc-13241658.title: Comparative evaluation of handwriting recognition by large language models (LLMs) in interpreting handwritten medication lists
pmc-13241658.creator: Tom G Jacobs, Laize Sílvia dos Anjos Botas Beca, Paul D van der Linden, Merel van Nuland
pmc-13241658.description: IntroductionHandwritten bedside medication lists remain common in healthcare, especially in low-resource countries, presenting challenges for digitization and automated safety checks. The introduction of large-language models may present an opportunity to facilitate digitization of handwritten medication lists.ObjectiveThis study evaluated the accuracy of three GPT-based language models in recognizing handwritten medication lists, presented in Dutch.

pmc-13262921.title: Hesperidin increases the in vitro anticancer activity of Pentagamavunon-1 in triple‐negative breast cancer with limited effects on normal cells
pmc-13262921.creator: Muthi Ikawati, Mila Hanifa, Nadzifa Nugraheni, Novia Permata Hapsari, Anif Nur Artanti, Dhania Novitasari, Rohmad Yudi Utomo, Mukh Syaifudin, Muchtaridi Muchtaridi, Endah Puji Septisetyani, Okid Parama Astirin, Edy Meiyanto
pmc-13262921.description: Pentagamavunon-1 (PGV-1) is a potential anticancer candidate due to its specific targeting of cancer cells with minimal toxicity to normal cells. This study examined the potency of hesperidin (HSD) in improving the anticancer effects of PGV-1 for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The 4T1 and NIH-3T3 cell lines were used as the model of TNBC and normal fibroblast, respectively.

pmc-13499099.title: Executive dysfunction and cognitive disorganization in schizophrenia: Case-control and cluster analyses of a Korean Wisconsin Card Sorting Test cohort
pmc-13499099.creator: Kyungwon Kim, Byung Dae Lee, Young Min Lee, Eunsoo Moon, Hwagyu Suh, Si Yul Kim
pmc-13499099.description: ObjectiveExecutive dysfunction is a hallmark cognitive deficit in schizophrenia, yet phenotypic heterogeneity within the disorder complicates clinical translation. This study aimed to identify discrete executive profiles within a large Korean schizophrenia cohort using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST) and to evaluate their clinical and functional correlates.MethodWe analyzed WCST performance in 276 individuals with schizophrenia and 361 healthy controls.

pmc-13602484.title: Mapping ICU nursing intervention notes to clinical care classification using a large language model: an evaluation study
pmc-13602484.creator: Yeonju Kim, Jiin Kim, Yunseong Cho, Mona Choi
pmc-13602484.description: BackgroundIntensive care unit (ICU) nurses often document their clinical concerns as free-text formats. The free-text documents pose significant challenges for transformation into quantifiable and standardized nursing data. Although large language models (LLMs) show promises in standardizing such documents, evidence supporting their application in nursing domain-specific tasks remains limited.

pmc-13651031.title: CoReGRN: a context-aware post-processing framework for gene regulatory network inference revealing regulatory signatures in HIV-Leishmaniasis
pmc-13651031.creator: Emma Paul M., Jereesh A. S., G. Santhosh Kumar
pmc-13651031.description: Accurate inference of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell gene expression data is challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and variability in gene-gene associations across cells. We propose CoReGRN (Contextual Refinement of Gene Regulatory Networks), a nonparametric, context-aware post-processing framework that refines inferred GRNs by reweighting candidate regulatory interactions using Mutual Information based association strength and local network context.
